page: Microsoft Azure E104id_v5 is an isolated, local-disk-equipped virtual machine instance belonging to the EIDv5 server family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 architecture server features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 104 vCPUs, derived from 52 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz and features 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 6.46 GB of memory per core, and includes 3891 GB of local storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core capabilities and high memory throughput. The instance achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 100873.26 and a Passmark CPU score of 79912.64, both placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Memory performance is a notable strength, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 5457.49 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 133.1 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is exceptionally high, as demonstrated by a top-tier Passmark CPU encryption test score of 94304.13. However, single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1709.0, and large-model LLM text generation is a relative bottleneck, yielding 2.62 tokens/sec on a 70B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E104id_v5 offers high resource density, combining substantial memory capacity with a large local storage allocation on a dedicated, isolated hardware profile. This balance makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive and data-heavy workloads. Recommended applications include large-scale database operations, high-throughput Redis caching layers, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks such as software compilation and decompression.
